item.title: UFL reaffirms customer commitment with nationwide independence draw
item.description: United Finance Limited [UFL] has awarded K51,000 in cash prizes to 81 customers across Papua New Guinea to mark the nation’s Independence anniversary. The nationwide Independence Cash Giveaway Promotion concluded with an official random draw conducted at the institution’s headquarters, where eligible clients were selected for cash rewards.
item.content:encoded:
United Finance Limited [UFL] has awarded K51,000 in cash prizes to 81 customers across Papua New Guinea to mark the nation’s Independence anniversary.

The nationwide Independence Cash Giveaway Promotion concluded with an official random draw conducted at the institution’s headquarters, where eligible clients were selected for cash rewards.

Under the prize distribution; 21 winners each received K1000 while 60 others got K500 each.

During the event, Client Retention and Compliance Team Leader Lavenda Konga drew the lucky winners for the Momase region.

UFL Group Media and Marketing Manager Hinuvi Onafimo said the promotion was designed to celebrate PNG’s independence while appreciating customer loyalty.

“As Papua New Guinea prepares to celebrate another year of independence, we are delighted to share this occasion with our customers,” Onafimo said.

“The promotion is our way of thanking our customers for their loyalty and support. We congratulate all the winners and encourage our customers to continue banking with confidence through United Finance.”

Onafimo said the high participation rate demonstrated growing confidence in UFL’s financial services.

He added that the company remains committed to providing accessible financial products for individuals, families, and businesses nationwide.

item.title: Middle Ramu MP devastated by plane crash
item.description: The Member for Middle Ramu, Kansol Kamdaru, says he is devastated over yesterday's tragic plane crash in his remote district, which claimed the lives of three people. The light aircraft operated by Niugini Aviation, was under the command of pilot Paul Gueme and his two passengers, had departed Mt Hagen soon after 1pm yesterday on a chartered run but met its fate about six miles south of Simbai.
item.content:encoded:
The Member for Middle Ramu, Kansol Kamdaru, says he is devastated over yesterday's tragic plane crash in his remote district, which claimed the lives of three people.

The light aircraft operated by Niugini Aviation, was under the command of pilot Paul Gueme and his two passengers, had departed Mt Hagen soon after 1pm yesterday on a chartered run but met its fate about six miles south of Simbai.

"I am so devastated to hear about the plane crash in my district. My people rely heavily on these third level aircrafts for their transportation needs, and what happened yesterday is a great loss to my district and my people," Kamdaru said.

"I also wish to express heartfelt condolences on behalf of my district and my people to the families and relatives of the three men who perished in the unfortunate incident. Our thoughts and prayers are with you all at this difficult time.

"Your loss is our loss too. Niugini Aviation has played a tremendous part in the lives of my people and contributed immensely to the development of Middle Ramu."

Former Madang Governor, Jim Kas, who is also a local man from Simbai, said Papua New Guinea has lost a great man, a very well experienced pilot, who did his job diligently, not for money but for the love of flying and contributing to the development of the remotest parts of this country.

"I have known the late pilot for a long time," Kas said.

"Knowing Paul, he loves flying and had the gist for the most difficult tasks. He understood the small people well and their needs, despite bad weather conditions, rugged terrains, and the remoteness of places. He took risks and flew across Papua New Guinea.

"He found happiness, satisfaction in serving the remote people. He knew the beauty of landing a plane in remote areas and seeing people smile when they see a plane land because that is their only connection to the outside world. Paul was the man in between, and he delivered it until yeaterday," Mr Kas said.

He also said that late Gueme flew in to Simbai three to four times a day until yesterday when he met his fate.

As a former leader for Madang, Kas also expressed sadness on his passing, as well as the two passengers.

"On behalf of the people of Middle Ramu, Raikos, and other remote areas of Madang Province that rely mostly on small aircrafts for their transportation needs, I would like to extend our deepest condolences to Paul's family, and the families of the two passengers who died in the tragic crash yesterday afternoon," he said.

item.content:encoded:
Two Police officers and a civilian have been arrested and charged for assisting in the recent mass jail break of 25 prisoners at the Wabag Police Station in Enga.

Acting Provincial Police Commander Chief Inspector Daniel Yangen said the officers have been arrested and charged with 22 indictable offences which includes aiding and abetting of the escapees. While the civilian was charged with aiding an escapee.

The three arrested were locked up at the Wabag Police Station without bail as they await court proceedings.

Chief Inspector Yangen has given orders to police prosecutors to produce the report on the prison escape. Meanwhile, the civilian is awaiting appropriate charges to be laid by police.

While that is going on Acting PPC Yangen has started awareness to apprehend the escapees, starting in Tsak Valley and at the Wapenamanda area.

He said it is important for the rule of law to take place whilst reminding leaders, magistrates and community members that they will be charged and arrested if found harboring and aiding these escapees and preventing justice to take its course.

The awareness follows an investigation on the issue by Internal Affairs.

So far, no prisoner of the 25 who escaped has been caught yet.

item.title: Popondetta festival keeps culture alive through music, dance and local talent
item.description: For three days, the streets of Popondetta came alive with music, dance and culture as communities gathered to celebrate the fourth annual Popondetta Arts and Music Festival. Held from September 4 to 6, the festival brought together local musicians, dancers, cultural performers and visiting artists, creating a platform for people to showcase their talents while keeping Oro’s cultural identity alive
item.content:encoded:
For three days, the streets of Popondetta came alive with music, dance and culture as communities gathered to celebrate the fourth annual Popondetta Arts and Music Festival.

Held from September 4 to 6, the festival brought together local musicians, dancers, cultural performers and visiting artists, creating a platform for people to showcase their talents while keeping Oro’s cultural identity alive.

For many local artists, the festival is more than a weekend of entertainment.

It provides an opportunity for emerging musicians and performers to step onto a bigger stage, connect with audiences and gain exposure while celebrating the culture and traditions of their communities.

International Solomon Islands artist Sean Rii joined some of PNG’s well-known performers, including Macdonald Taylor, Anslom Nakikus and Tarvin Toune, to entertain festival-goers.

The G-Force Dance Crew from Port Moresby also added colour and energy to the event with dynamic performances that captivated the Popondetta crowd.

But beyond the headline performances, it was the participation of local artists that gave the festival its cultural heartbeat.

Local musicians and performers from Oro took to the stage with old favourites and new songs, demonstrating the depth of talent within the province and giving younger performers an opportunity to see that their creativity can take them beyond their communities.

The festival also serves as a reminder that cultural preservation does not only happen in museums or through traditional ceremonies.

It can happen through music, dance, storytelling, performance and the active participation of young people.

By bringing generations together through the arts, the festival is helping create space for local culture to be shared, appreciated and passed on.

The National Cultural Commission, through the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture, has recognised and supported the event, which was first initiated in 2023.

This year's festival was fully funded through the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture, through the National Cultural Commission, with support from the Popondetta District Development Authority under the leadership of local MP Richard Masere.

The partnerships have helped strengthen the festival as a platform for cultural expression, tourism and the development of local creative talent.

As the Popondetta Arts and Music Festival continues to grow, its significance extends beyond the stage.

It is becoming a space where people can celebrate who they are, where artists can tell their stories through their craft, and where younger generations can experience and carry forward the culture of Oro.

For Popondetta, the festival is not simply getting bigger and better but it is becoming part of the community's effort to keep its culture, creativity and identity alive for the next generation.

item.title: Moresby South women praise new Kaugere festival initiative
item.description: Women in the Moresby South electorate have commended local MP Justin Tkatchenko following the launch of the Kaugere Music and Market Festival. The initiative provides a dedicated platform for women and youths in Kaugere to showcase their musical talents while selling local goods, including food, arts, and crafts.
item.content:encoded:
Women in the Moresby South electorate have commended local MP Justin Tkatchenko following the launch of the Kaugere Music and Market Festival.

The initiative provides a dedicated platform for women and youths in Kaugere to showcase their musical talents while selling local goods, including food, arts, and crafts.

Kaugere Women’s Association Coordinator Susan Kaia said the event was particularly timely as Papua New Guinea prepares for its upcoming 51st Independence anniversary.

"This event was initiated because we wanted to come out openly to showcase our talents and skills, and to highlight what we do in our communities," Kaia said.

"This is the first time an event of this kind has come to us. Thank you to the sponsor, the Honorable Justin Tkatchenko, for always supporting us here at Kaugere Southside."

Despite low initial turnout from buyers, Kaia said that vendors remained enthusiastic about the opportunity to participate.

"Although we didn't have a large number of customers turn up to buy food, crafts, or dresses, we didn't give up. We still came to showcase our talents and skills, and we are happy," Kaia said. "Since this is our first time, we hope to make it even better in the future."

item.title: 50th jubilee celebrations launched for Kerema diocese
item.description: The Kerema Catholic Diocese launched its 50th Golden Jubilee Anniversary Celebrations in Kerema Town on Saturday. Parishioners from all the 11 parishes across Gulf, traveled into the provincial capital on Saturday, to witness this historic milestone for the church.
item.content:encoded:
The Kerema Catholic Diocese launched its 50th Golden Jubilee Anniversary Celebrations in Kerema Town on Saturday.

Parishioners from all the 11 parishes across Gulf, traveled into the provincial capital on Saturday, to witness this historic milestone for the church.

Catholic faithfuls from the parishes gathered at the Kerema Catholic Diocese Church for a special Thanksgiving Mass, which was led by Bishop Baquero, to mark the launch of the Jubilee year.

"The 50th anniversary is a time to reflect on the past, celebrate the present, and renew the commitment of spreading the Gospel in the years ahead," Baquero said.

The celebrations will be held under the theme: 'Alive in Christ, Journeying Together, and Proclaiming the Gospel with Love and Mercy'.

Due to limited spacing at the Diocese grounds, smaller celebrations will be held at each individual parish throughout the province, during the year.

Each parish was also given a Jubilee Cross to take back and continue the celebrations in their own communities.

item.title: Police rescue female hostage, seven shot dead
item.description: Seven armed kidnappers have been shot dead and one hostage rescued in a dawn police operation in Haiyafuli village, Western province. The event took place at the Bedamuni rural area near Mogulu in the Middle Fly District, over the weekend following the kidnapping of two women.
item.content:encoded:
Seven armed kidnappers have been shot dead and one hostage rescued in a dawn police operation in Haiyafuli village, Western province.

The event took place at the Bedamuni rural area near Mogulu in the Middle Fly District, over the weekend following the kidnapping of two women.

This was revealed by the Border Commander Acting Commissioner of Police Steven Francis when contacted by NBC News.

ACP Francis said North Fly police moved in at 6:30am on Saturday after tracking an armed group that had demanded K150,000 ransom for two women that were abducted from Fuma village.

"Police were inserted at Uruamabi on Saturday 5th September. From there they walked all the way to Fuma village and than walk up to Haiyafuli where the gang group were in the early hours of the morning. Upon seeing the police the gang gun fire to police and they exchange fire," he said.

Francis said the group originally had 11 members. Three others left for Komo the previous day and remain at large whilst the other eight where with the victims at Haiyafuli Village.

He said police held surveillance through the night and moved in when one hostage managed to create distance between herself and the captors.

From the eight, one was shot and killed on the spot during the police shootout. Six others were shot and later died after falling off from a cliff while trying to escape. Another suspect escaped unharmed.

ACP Francis confirmed that one hostage escaped during the exchange of gunfire and has since been reunited with her family.

Sadly, the second hostage was still inside the house when police entered. ACP Francis said she was attacked and killed by one of the kidnappers before she could be rescued.

Following the operation, police recovered three homemade shotguns and two rounds of ammunition from the scene.

item.title: National HPV vaccination launched
item.description: A new national Human Papillomavirus [HPV] vaccination program has been officially launched in Port Moresby as part of efforts to protect children, especially girls aged 9 to 14 years, from cervical cancer. Health Secretary Pascoe Kase announced that the rollout will begin in the National Capital District before expanding to other provinces across the country.
item.content:encoded:
A new national Human Papillomavirus [HPV] vaccination program has been officially launched in Port Moresby as part of efforts to protect children, especially girls aged 9 to 14 years, from cervical cancer.

Health Secretary Pascoe Kase announced that the rollout will begin in the National Capital District before expanding to other provinces across the country.

The program is a partnership between the National Department of Health and the Department of Education. It is supported by GAVI, the World Health Organization, UNICEF, and the governments of PNG and Australia.

According to Kase, the vaccine has already been administered to more than 1 billion people in over 150 countries and is proven to be safe and effective.

“We want to reach every child, in school and out of school, who have not had the opportunity to be protected. Schools, teachers, health workers and communities all have a role to play in making this program a success,” he said.

Community health teams will be deployed to each location to educate parents and provide information on how the vaccine works. Parents are being encouraged to ask questions and support their children to get vaccinated.

Meanwhile, the NCD Provincial Health Authority is leading the first phase of the national program.

NCD PHA chief executive officer Dr. Robin Oge said vaccination activities will start in Port Moresby before moving into schools across the district.

Dr. Oge acknowledged the support of the National Department of Health, Department of Education, GAVI and WHO.

He also cited recent health data showing that around 1,300 women die from cervical cancer in PNG each year, and said vaccination is the most effective way to prevent future deaths.

He said NCD PHA teams will go into schools and communities to deliver the vaccine and provide awareness to parents. The authority is targeting 80% coverage in NCD.

“This vaccine is about protecting our daughters, our sisters, for the future. We are calling on parents, teachers and communities to support this program and allow our children to be vaccinated.”

Dr. Oge called on parents, teachers and communities to support the program to ensure no child is left behind in the fight against cervical cancer.

The rollout is expected to continue in other centers following today’s launch in NCD.

item.title: Pacific leaders urged to keep Bougainville issue internal
item.description: Pacific Islands Forum [PIF] leaders have been urged not to treat the Bougainville referendum as a regional matter, with key officials emphasizing that it remains an internal political process for Papua New Guinea to resolve.

item.title: Madang plane crash claims 3 lives
item.description: A third-level airline, operated by Niugini Aviation, reportedly went down yesterday afternoon, killing three people instantly, including the national pilot.
